spec_features.spec_quote: It is capped (`max_nudges=1` by default) so we don't badger the model into artifacts
spec_features.evidence: config.py:31 `max_nudges: int = 1`; agent.py:96 `if cfg.nudge_on_premature_done and nudges < cfg.max_nudges and not _verify(...)` and agent.py:119 same guard; `nudges += 1` (agent.py:97,121) increments so once the cap is hit no further nudge is appended/sent. The re-contact is genuinely bounded and the limit changes execution (loop stops nudging).
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked in BOTH the no-tool-call path and the post-finish path. Default 1 means at most one re-contact.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If the agent says it is done but task is unsolved, optionally nudge it once more to expose abandonment vs. persistence behavior. (config.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Three independent caps, checked at the top of every loop iteration
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:56-66 at top of `while True`: `if step_no >= cfg.max_steps: ... break`; `if time.time() - start > cfg.max_wall_time_s: ... break`; `if t.total_tokens_in + t.total_tokens_out > cfg.max_total_tokens: ... break`. total_tokens are accumulated in Transcript.add() (schemas.py:52-55) from real API usage (models.py:82-83,115-116), so all three caps compare real data and break the loop, recording a finish_reason.
spec_features.notes: All three are enforced end-to-end and set distinct finish_reason values (max_steps/timeout/killed).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: """Limits on the agent loop. Doubles as a kill switch.""" (config.py:23); agent.py comments label these as `# ---- kill switch checks ----` and `kill switch: ...` meta events

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not optimize the agent into distress, we cap re-contact (nudges)
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as max_nudges: agent.py:96 and 119 gate nudges with `nudges < cfg.max_nudges`; re-contact is bounded to max_nudges (default 1). No code path optimizes toward distress; the only re-contact is the single capped nudge.
spec_features.notes: This is the same enforced cap; the 'do not optimize into distress' part is just the absence of any distress-optimizing code, not a positive mechanism.
